license: CC-BY (version unspecified in NIH source metadata)
note: NIAID's existing SARS-CoV-2 teaching model from NIH 3D, reused without any geometry or material changes. The source combines imaging-informed modeling with authored surface and spike placement; it is not an unmodified single-particle reconstruction. The complete model, including spikes, has its longest source span displayed at the cube root of the listed representative volume (an equivalent-volume span). This is not an enclosed mesh-volume measurement or a calibrated lipid-envelope volume. The separate Length entry retains its original envelope-diameter calibration.

operations: Download SARSCOV2_Thick_NIH3D.glb from NIH 3D (submission 17182, run 20e70d77-195b-4032-bb74-2a8c59184a43, output-file 386420)
gltf-transform simplify --ratio 0.09 --error 0.01 (566,399 -> 50,522 triangles, vertex colors preserved through decimation)

Measured envelope vs. full extent with a custom script (measure_corona.py) that classifies vertices by COLOR_0 (teal/blue = envelope, pale = spikes, orange = HE/membrane proteins) and compares mean envelope radius to overall bounding-box extent

volume_calibration.method: Longest native source span normalized to 1, so displayed span is V^(1/3). Equivalent-span illustration only; no enclosed, material or capacity volume measured.
